title: Strategic customer workshop playbook - POC & deployment
content:
Purpose
This playbook is a facilitation-ready agenda, slide-outline, and set of facilitation notes for a 3-hour customer workshop focused on scoping a Redwood Inference POC, aligning on deployment requirements (hosted / dedicated / private), and generating an actionable runbook and next-step commitments. Use this when an AE + SE pair needs to convert an exploratory conversation into a concrete pilot and deployment proposal.

Goals (what success looks like)
- Shared understanding of the customer’s core inference workload, SLOs (latency & throughput), and data constraints.
- Agreed POC scope with measurable success criteria (latency targets, cost objectives, functional tests).
- Preliminary architecture decision: hosted vs dedicated vs private + list of integration touchpoints.
- Owner assignments and a 30/60/90 day POC plan.

Attendees (recommended)
- Customer: 1x engineering lead, 1x ML engineer, 1x product manager, 1x security/compliance rep (if applicable)
- Redwood: Solutions Engineer (facilitator), AE (commercial), Infra SE (optional deep dive), Customer Success (onboarding lead)

Pre-work to send 3 business days before workshop
- Short intake form for customer to complete (model types, expected qps, average/peak sequence lengths, sample prompts, data residency constraints).
- Lightweight run of a Redwood quick-bench with sample prompt set (SE-run): collect token counts, sample latencies.
- Share the workshop agenda and a one-page POC checklist.

3-hour workshop agenda (timeboxed)
0:00–0:10 Welcome & objectives (SE)
- Quick intros and roles
- Confirm workshop goals and desired outcomes
- Review timebox and where we will capture decisions (Confluence POC page)

0:10–0:35 Customer context & current architecture (Customer leads)
- Customer walks through current model(s), infra, and pain points (15 min)
- Clarifying questions from Redwood (10 min)
- Key artifacts: current infra diagram, SLA/latency expectations, cost constraints

0:35–1:05 Redwood capability overview & relevant patterns (SE)
- 10 min: Short slides: runtime features (batching, KV cache, quantization, routing)
- 20 min: Reference patterns for: low-latency interactive, high-throughput batch, regulated private deployments

1:05–1:25 Interactive exercise: workload profile & tradeoffs (workshop)
- SE presents 3 small workload profiles (chat-bot interactive, document-embedding pipeline, reranking).
- Breakout: customer maps their workload to a profile and lists top constraints (10 min).
- Group share: call out biggest risks and immediate unknowns (10 min).

1:25–1:40 Break

1:40–2:10 Architecture options and recommended POC plan (SE + Infra SE)
- Walk through 3 recommended architecture options with quick TCO and SLO implications: hosted API pilot, dedicated reserved pool POC, private VPC trial. (20 min)
- Each option shows: network integration points, data flow, security controls, expected token cost ranges, latency expectations.

2:10–2:40 Hands-on scenario: model routing & fallback policy exercise (interactive)
- Present a short decision matrix: latency-first vs cost-first vs regulated data-first.
- Workshop asks customer to design policy for: 1) normal load 2) capacity shortage 3) degraded model quality. (20 min)
- SE takes notes and synthesizes a recommended fallback policy.

2:40–2:55 Success criteria & instrumentation plan (SE + CS)
- Define measurable tests for POC (latency percentiles, throughput, functional correctness on prompts)
- Observability checklist: tracing hooks, token-level cost monitoring, quality regression alerts, sample set for evals

2:55–3:00 Next steps, owners, and close (AE + SE)
- Confirm POC kick-off date, immediate blockers, contract needs, and support contacts
- Capture follow-ups in Confluence and JIRA (assign owners)

Slide deck outline (10–12 slides)
1. Title, goal & agenda (1 slide)
2. Customer context summary (1)
3. Redwood quick capabilities snapshot (1)
4. Reference deployment patterns (1)
5. Workload profile & where the customer maps (1)
6. Architecture options with pros/cons (2 slides)
7. Hands-on policy exercise template (1)
8. POC success criteria & instrumentation (1)
9. 30/60/90 POC plan and milestones (1)
10. Risks, mitigations, and decision log (1)
11. Next steps & owners (1)

Facilitation notes & scripts (practical tips)
- Kickoff: set expectations about decisions vs. explorations. If the group is large, ask non-essential participants to silently observe.
- Timeboxing: call out the time and purpose at the start of each segment. Use the parking-lot for off-topic deep dives.
- Eliciting constraints: when customer is vague on SLOs, ask for specific percentile-based targets (p50, p95). If they don’t have numbers, use "acceptable" vs "deal-breaker" prompts.
- Handling security/compliance participants: highlight private deployment options early, surface KMS/HSM support and audit log retention options.
- During the hands-on policy exercise, capture decisions in a simple table: trigger -> action -> owner.

Templates to populate during the workshop
- POC decision table: objective | metric | pass threshold | test plan | owner
- Integration checklist: API endpoints, auth method, VPC peering, network egress expectations, IP allowlist
- Observability checklist: tracing, per-request token cost, p95 latency alarms, sample prompt evaluation harness

Common risks and suggested mitigations
- Risk: Customer unknowns about peak load. Mitigation: define a short load-profiling step in week 1 of the POC using synthetic traffic.
- Risk: Data residency/regulatory blockers. Mitigation: propose an initial hosted pilot limited to anonymized prompts or a Dedicated/VPC trial.
- Risk: Quality regression after quantization. Mitigation: include a quality gate test on a representative prompt set before switching quantized runtime.

Artifacts to produce after the session (owners & timeline)
- Confluence POC page (SE, within 48 hours): architecture notes, decision log, success criteria, runbook
- JIRA epic + tickets (AE + SE, within 72 hours): POC tasks, infra setup, tests, contract items
- Proposal draft (AE, within 5 business days): pricing for chosen option + optional add-ons (observability retention, SLA uplift)

30/60/90 day POC milestones (example)
- Day 0–7: Kickoff, infra provisioning, sample traffic run, baseline latency/cost measurements
- Day 8–30: Feature testing, onboarding, iterating model/quantization profiles, observability instrumentation
- Day 31–90: Load validation, final regression checks, rollout plan and contract conversion discussion

Follow-up checklist for SEs after workshop
- Immediately: create Confluence page with decisions and tag CS & AE
- 24–48h: schedule technical kickoff with Infra SE to provision any dedicated capacity or VPC networking
- 72h: share proposal/pricing and POC ticketing with customer
- Weekly: 30-min syncs to measure against success criteria and adjust config

Appendix: quick prompts for eliciting key data
- What is your current p95 latency objective for user-facing flows?
- Average token length of requests and expected concurrency?
- Any restrictions on storing request/response logs? Retention windows?
- Are there regulatory needs for on-premises processing or specific cloud regions?
- Can you share a representative set of 50 prompts we can use for quality tests?

Notes to facilitator
- Save at least 10–15 minutes at the end for blockers and contractual questions; AEs often need that time.
- If the customer is strongly cost-sensitive, prioritize showing a tangible TCO comparison between hosted and dedicated for their profile.
- Keep the handbook accessible as a living Confluence page and attach the filled templates there after the session.
